recommendation: Keep this no-change audit commit. Revisit only if HL7 later decides to replace the stable hl7.org/fhir-issues alias with direct jira.hl7.org URLs throughout the specification; that would be a new link-policy cleanup rather than missing application of FHIR-19334.
issue_request: FHIR-19334 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and requested changing FHIR specification links from the old HL7 wiki and gForge tracker to Confluence and Jira.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites GH#512a4d9c8. That merge, "Merge pull request #270 from HL7/confluence-jira", broadly replaced wiki spreadsheet-authoring links with Confluence links, removed generic gForge tracker references, and introduced the stable http://hl7.org/fhir-issues tracker link for generic issue submission.
additional_context: A contemporaneous Zulip committers thread from Lloyd McKenzie explained the migration strategy: generic gForge change-proposal links intentionally became http://hl7.org/fhir-issues so that alias could redirect to Jira when ready; specific tracker links became Jira paths; and old wiki references were given Confluence placeholders. Current source still intentionally uses Confluence/Jira guidance and the hl7.org/fhir-issues alias.
reconciliation: No source changes were made. The focused current-source scan found no remaining wiki.hl7.org, gforge.hl7.org, or tracker.fhir.org links targeted by this issue; the only hit was a historical Argonaut wiki link in source/history.html, outside the FHIR wiki/tracker infrastructure migration.
